tools.description: Noul: answer one bounded yes/no question with TypeSafe and return a probability from 0 to 1. Pass state as text or a JSON-encoded object/array string; encode structured state into the string, not a native object, and prefer named fields for multi-part state. instructions is the yes/no question and must carry the complete meaning; criteria_true and criteria_false are optional. Noul returns only the probability and has no confidence field: one Noul answers one label, so issue one Noul per label when several may each apply, and a value near 0.5 means yes and no are similarly likely, not medium intensity. Report the probability as returned. Not for open-ended generation.

state.description: Text to evaluate, or a JSON-encoded object or array string. Structured state must be encoded into this string, not passed as a native object or array; prefer named fields for multi-part state.

instructions.description: The yes/no question the decision must answer, carrying its complete meaning.

criteria_true.description: Optional description of what a true (yes) answer means.

criteria_false.description: Optional description of what a false (no) answer means.

tools.description: Choice: select one option from a bounded, mutually exclusive rubric with TypeSafe. Pass criteria as a JSON-encoded string (not a native object) whose content is a JSON object mapping each option key to a short description or null, for example "{\"bug\": \"a defect\", \"feature\": null}". Include a no-match option when nothing may fit. The result choice is one of the criteria keys and probabilities sum to 1 over the same keys as competing options; confidence is distribution concentration, not correctness. Use one Noul per label instead when several labels may each apply. Do not use for open-ended generation.

state.description: Text to evaluate, or a JSON-encoded object or array string. Structured state must be encoded into this string, not passed as a native object or array; prefer named fields for multi-part state.

instructions.description: The bounded choice question the decision must answer, carrying its complete meaning.

criteria.description: A JSON-encoded string, not a native object. Its content is a JSON object mapping each option key to a short rubric description or null. Example: "{\"bug\": \"a defect\", \"feature\": null}". Values must be strings or null.

tools.description: Score: place state on an ordered rubric with TypeSafe and return a probability-weighted position. Pass criteria as a JSON-encoded string (not a native array) whose content is a JSON array of 2 to 10 concrete, self-standing level descriptions, for example "[\"poor\", \"acceptable\", \"excellent\"]". The returned score and probability keys are zero-based rubric indexes; map them to labels with legend and do not add 1. probabilities sum to 1 across the levels and confidence is distribution concentration, not correctness. For graded ranking, score every candidate with the same comparable rubric and sort in code.

state.description: Text to evaluate, or a JSON-encoded object or array string. Structured state must be encoded into this string, not passed as a native object or array; prefer named fields for multi-part state.

instructions.description: The scoring question the decision must answer, carrying its complete meaning.

criteria.description: A JSON-encoded string, not a native array. Its content is a JSON array of 2 to 10 concrete, self-standing level descriptions. Example: "[\"poor\", \"acceptable\", \"excellent\"]". Do not use objects such as {"level": 1, "label": "..."}.
